end.summary:
Practised multiplying by 10 and 100 using place value and zero patterns.
Sameer explained that multiplying by 10 shifts each digit one place and solved 125 × 10 = 1,250.
Solved 125 × 100 = 12,500 and 36 × 100 = 3,600.
Used doubling to solve 36 × 4 = 144 and worked through 25 × 24 = 600.
The doubling-and-halving method for 25 × 36 remained partly unclear; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Sameer practised place value for multiplying by 10 and 100, including explaining why zeros are added. They also used repeated doubling and checked a result by dividing by 4. The 25 × 36 doubling-and-halving method was still mixed up at the end, so it was not fully corrected. At home, practise one example such as 25 × 16 by doubling 25 to 50 while halving 16 to 8, then repeat the steps aloud.
